result.text: Consider a process for purchasing items from an online shop.
The user starts an order by logging in to their account.
Then, the user simultaneously selects the items to purchase and sets a payment method.
Afterward, the user either pays or completes an installment agreement.
After selecting the items, the user chooses between multiple options for a free reward.
Since the reward value depends on the purchase value, this step is done after selecting the items, but it is independent of the payment activities.
Finally, the items are delivered.
The user has the right to return items for exchange.
Every time items are returned, a new delivery is made.

result.process_description:
Consider a process for purchasing items from an online shop.
The user starts an order by logging in to their account.
Then, the user simultaneously selects the items to purchase and sets a payment method.
Afterward, the user either pays or completes an installment agreement.
After selecting the items, the user chooses between multiple options for a free reward.
Since the reward value depends on the purchase value, this step is done after selecting the items, but it is independent of the payment activities.
Finally, the items are delivered.
The user has the right to return items for exchange.
Every time items are returned, a new delivery is made.

args.text: When the description says activities happen simultaneously, or says an activity is independent of another, model the concurrent branches with a parallel gateway and synchronize them before any later activity that depends on both branches.

trace.reason: Check existing documented guidance about explicitly concurrent and independent activities before classifying the proposed guideline.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.

args.text: When the description says that each occurrence of an activity or condition causes a later activity to be performed again, model the repetition with a loop or a decision gateway and a sequence flow back to the repeated activity.

Represent loops only when repetition is stated and provide a meaningful exit unless endless behavior is explicit.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.

args.text: When a description states that activities happen simultaneously, or that an activity is independent of another but must occur after a particular prerequisite, model the concurrent branches with parallel gateways, joining or synchronizing them only where the description requires it.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers the concurrent activities and their dependencies.

result.rule: When the description states that several activities are all required before a later activity or outcome: Model the activities as parallel branches and synchronize all branches with a parallel gateway before the later activity or outcome.

When the description says an activity may or may not occur before a later required activity: model the optional activity as one branch of an exclusive gateway, and merge the branches before the later required activity

When the description explicitly orders activities or says that work continues until a stated condition is reached: Model the activities in the stated sequence, and do not represent them as parallel or mutually exclusive branches unless the description explicitly supports concurrency or a decision.

When the description says an optional activity may occur after an outcome, and each occurrence is followed by another specified activity: Model the optional activity as a task on one branch of an exclusive gateway, with the other branch ending or continuing as described; connect the activity back to the specified later activity when it must follow each occurrence.
